schemaConversionRootCause.symptom: Transform schema conversion failed instantly (job FAILED) both jobs; DMS metadata import via --refresh returned 'Unexpected application error'; conversion returned 'No metadata models matched'.
schemaConversionRootCause.CORRECTED_rootCause: The ONLY deterministic root cause was the SELECTION RULE: rule-action=explicit with schema-name='%'. Under 'explicit', '%' is a LITERAL (not a wildcard), so it matched nothing -> 'No metadata models matched'. Correct rule: explicit + server-name + database-name (omit schema-name = entire DB), OR rule-action=include + wildcard '%'. This was a mistake in my hand-written CLI rule.

CONTROLLED TEST DISPROVED IT: import on the ORIGINAL public-IP project WGX5 with the CORRECT rule = SUCCESS (req ad142e22). The public instance profile is NOT a blocker. The private instance profile atx-sc-clean-ip I created was UNNECESSARY.

directCodeTransformation.cutoverNote: Verified path uses EF EnsureCreated -> tables created by EF in 'public' schema with EF (PascalCase, quoted) naming. The DMS-converted DDL (Route 1) creates schema 'bobsusedbookstore_dbo' with lowercase names. For a real cutover reusing the DMS schema, either (a) let EF own the schema (EnsureCreated/migrations, drop DMS DDL), or (b) add HasDefaultSchema('bobsusedbookstore_dbo') + explicit lowercase table/column mappings to match DMS output (PG is case-sensitive on quoted identifiers, unlike SQL Server).
